explication:
<explanation>
1. Project Type & Purpose  
   - Piwigo is a monolithic, full-stack PHP web application: an open-source photo-gallery platform.  
   - It serves web clients (browsers) and provides both a user-facing gallery and an admin interface, plus a REST/WS API.

2. High-Level Architecture Components  
   a. Clients & Front Door  
      • End-user browsers (UI)  
      • Optionally a load balancer or reverse proxy (nginx/HAProxy)  
   b. Web Tier  
      • Apache or nginx + PHP-FPM  
      • PHP application (index.php, admin.php, action.php, ws.php)  
      • Smarty template engine (include/smarty)  
      • Plugins directory (extend core functionality)  
      • Themes directory (UI customization)  
   c. Storage Tier  
      • Relational database (MySQL/MariaDB)  
        – Schema managed by install/db scripts & upgrade scripts  
      • File storage for uploaded images + derivatives (/galleries, /derivative)  
      • Cache (filesystem-based thumbnail cache)  
   d. Services  
      • Image processing (GD or ImageMagick) invoked by derivative.inc.php  
      • Mail (PHPMailer) for notifications  
      • Web services API (JSON, XML-RPC) under include/ws_protocols  
   e. Optional Infrastructure  
      • CDN for static assets (themes/js, themes/images, galleries)  
      • Object storage (S3-compatible) in place of local file system  
      • Redis/Memcached for session or query caching  

3. Interactions & Data Flow  
   1. Browser → HTTP(S) request to load-balancer/ reverse-proxy  
   2. Proxy → Web server (nginx/Apache) → PHP-FPM  
   3. PHP Router (index.php/admin.php/ws.php) directs to controllers in include/*.php  
   4. Controllers read/write data via DB layer (include/dblayer/functions_*.inc.php)  
   5. Controllers invoke business logic (functions_*.inc.php), image processing (derivative.inc.php), plugin hooks  
   6. Data is passed to Smarty templates for HTML rendering and returned to browser  
   7. On image upload: PHP stores original file in galleries/ and generates cached thumbnails in derivative/  
   8. Notifications use PHPMailer → external SMTP  
   9. API calls (ws.php) use include/ws_protocols to serialize responses in JSON/XML/etc.

4. Architectural Patterns & Design Principles  
   - Monolithic MVC-like structure: separation of concerns via includes/controllers, templates, and assets  
   - Plugin hooks allow extensibility without core changes  
   - Template engine (Smarty) cleanly separates PHP logic from presentation  
   - DB migrations for schema evolution (install/db, upgrade_*.php)  

5. Diagramming Guidelines Tailored to Piwigo  
   - Draw a block for “Clients (Browser/App)” on the left  
   - Add a box labeled “Load Balancer / Reverse Proxy” (optional)  
   - Draw one or more “Web Server + PHP-FPM” nodes  
   - Inside that box, subdivide:  
     • Core PHP Application (entry scripts → includes/controllers)  
     • Smarty Template Engine  
     • Plugins & Themes (illustrate as side modules)  
     • WS/API Layer (JSON/XMLRPC endpoints)  
   - On the right, show “MySQL / MariaDB” and “File Storage” (galleries/, derivative/)  
   - Underneath, depict “Image Processing Service (GD/ImageMagick)” and “SMTP Service” as external services  
   - Optionally show “Cache Layer” (filesystem/Redis) and “CDN”  

6. Visual Details  
   - Use clear rectangular shapes for components (web servers, DB, storage)  
   - Use cylinders for databases and object storage  
   - Use cloud icons for external services (SMTP, CDN)  
   - Draw directional arrows for HTTP requests, DB queries, file reads/writes, API calls  
   - Color-code:  
     • Green for core application  
     • Blue for data stores  
     • Orange for external dependencies/services  
     • Gray for optional infrastructure (CDN, cache)  

7. Key Diagram Elements to Include  
   - Labels: component name + main technologies (e.g., “Web Server (nginx + PHP-FPM)”)  
   - Data flows: HTTP(s), SQL, file I/O, API payloads  
   - Extensibility points: Plugins folder, Themes folder, WS/API interfaces  
   - Migration scripts: illustrate DB schema management under “install/db & upgrade”  

By following these guidelines, you’ll produce a detailed, accurate architecture diagram of the Piwigo system—highlighting its monolithic PHP core, database/storage interactions, template engine, extensibility points, and external service integrations.
